title: Bounded flat comparison for the explicit ordinary coefficient tensor complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring in the scheme universe, $d$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and $P$ an $A$-module cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] strictly supported in an integer interval $[a,b]$, with every term flat. Use ordinary completed constant realization $H$ and the explicit ordinary coefficient tensor construction [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-free-tensor-cone], so $C=H(P)$ and $T_n=C\otimes_{A_T}(A/I^{n+1})_T$, with actual coefficient transition maps. Choose any left adjoints $L_n$ to the exact derived quotient restrictions. Then the levelwise localization $Q(T)$ is isomorphic, as a whole diagram, to the canonical derived quotient diagram of $Q(P)$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-perfect-adic-quotient-diagram] followed by completed derived constant realization. Moreover $Q(C)$ is isomorphic to the completed derived constant realization of $Q(P)$. No projectivity or finiteness of the terms is assumed.

proof.text: Use ordinary completed scalar-extension exactness and the natural coefficient tensor balancing comparison. Compose with exact constant realization to obtain exact H. Apply the comparison degreewise to P and transpose complexes of diagrams to diagrams of complexes; localization commutes with H by its exact derived factorization.

A strictly bounded-above complex of flat A-modules is K-flat. The explicit algebraic level maps are therefore invertible. Consecutive naturality of those prescribed maps assembles a natural transformation by NatTrans.ofOpSequence. Objectwise invertibility gives a diagram isomorphism, including every transition.

Exact completed scalar extension E has its exact derived functor E.mapDerivedCategory as a left derived functor. Its selected completed derived extension has the universal left-derived comparison supplied by the normalized scalar-extension data. Uniqueness of left derived functors identifies these two functors. The exact derived composition isomorphism for constant realization followed by E identifies H.mapDerivedCategory with the prescribed completed derived realization. Whisker the algebraic diagram isomorphism with this exact derived H and compose the degreewise comparisons for the first conclusion. The exact factorization at P and the same derived-composition comparison give the cone-point isomorphism. Only the upper bound is used; the original statement and both bound binders stay unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem finitePerfectAdicFlatTensor_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (L : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{t} (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))))
    (adj : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⊣ DerivedCategory.adicLevelRestriction d.ideal n)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{t} A) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
    (ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Flat A (P.X i)) :
    Nonempty (finitePerfectAdicTensorComplexDiagram X d P ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅
      finitePerfectAdicQuotientDiagram d.ideal L adj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ⋙
        finitePerfectAdicDerivedConstant X A ⋙
          completedAdicDerivedChange X (completedAdicScalar X d)) ∧
    Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (finitePerfectAdicOrdinaryComplex X d P) ≅
      (completedAdicDerivedChange X (completedAdicScalar X d)).obj
        ((finitePerfectAdicDerivedConstant X A).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)))
